question: Should OpenClaw expose a configurable exec approval timeout, and if so what canonical key, bounds, and precedence should it use?
rationale: Adding this knob changes a host-exec authorization window and creates public config surface, so automation should not pick key naming, maximum duration, or env/config precedence without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add bounded canonical config
options.body: Expose one documented timeout key with conservative minimum/maximum validation and wire it through all exec approval request and wait paths.

options.title: Keep fixed default
options.body: Decline the public knob and keep the current 30-minute default, possibly improving UX around missed approvals instead.

options.title: Config-only, no env var
options.body: Allow `openclaw.json` control but avoid a process-wide environment override for this security-sensitive window.

recommendation.title: Add bounded canonical config
recommendation.body: Expose one documented timeout key with conservative minimum/maximum validation and wire it through all exec approval request and wait paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the clearest feature-history connection to the shared exec approval timeout and routing behavior.
